title: Add merkle_frontier field to audit_signed_tree_heads table

story.i_want_to: persist the merkle frontier (path needed for incremental computation) alongside each STH, so that future STH computations can fold only new entries instead of recomputing the entire chain
story.so_that: STH computation becomes O(new entries) instead of O(total history), reducing per-minute CPU and database load quadratically as the audit chain grows

rationale: Currently, ComputeSthWorker recomputes the entire merkle tree for a tenant every minute by fetching all entry hashes from genesis and rebuilding the tree top-to-bottom. This is O(total_chain_size) per minute per tenant. Merkle-tree incremental computation requires persisting the frontier (the set of hashes needed to attach new entries to the previous root). The frontier is derivable from the tree structure and is ~log(chain_size) in size, so storing it enables O(new_entries) computation on the next cycle.

acceptance_criteria.description: A new migration (timestamp, create_add_merkle_frontier_to_sth) adds a nullable :binary column `merkle_frontier` to the `audit_signed_tree_heads` table
The `Loopctl.AuditChain.SignedTreeHead` schema includes the new `merkle_frontier` field with type :binary
The SignedTreeHead changeset casts `merkle_frontier` as optional (not required)
Existing STH queries and tests pass without modification (merkle_frontier defaults to nil for existing rows)
New STHs created during this task do not yet populate merkle_frontier (left as nil); this field will be populated by US-35.2

test_cases.name: SignedTreeHead schema accepts merkle_frontier
steps: Create a SignedTreeHead changeset with merkle_frontier = <<...some binary...>>
expected_results: merkle_frontier is present in the changes

test_cases.name: SignedTreeHead stores and retrieves merkle_frontier
steps: Insert a SignedTreeHead with merkle_frontier = some_binary
expected_results: merkle_frontier is persisted and retrieved correctly

test_cases.name: Existing STHs have nil merkle_frontier after migration
steps: Query the STH from the database

notes: This is a foundational schema change; US-35.2 depends on it. Keep the changeset backward-compatible (merkle_frontier optional) so existing code paths don't break during the migration window.
